page: Microsoft Azure D48als_v7 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Allocated under Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, along with SHA-NI and AES extensions. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and includes no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional CPU computation capability. The instance placed in the top tier (top 10%) for Geekbench single-core (2,796.0) and multi-core (24,978.0) performance, as well as stress-ng single-core execution (3,662.37). Cryptographic and compression workloads show similar strength, achieving 40.97 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 18.08 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In PassMark tests, the CPU score reached 76,718.92, placing in the top 25%. Instruction-level optimizations benefit software compilation, image processing, and ray tracing, all scoring in the top quartile.

Memory and operational throughput metrics reflect strong bandwidth characteristics, recording 4,932.63 GB/sec in cached small-block reads and 102.58 GB/sec in large-block writes. Static web serving throughput reaches 58.83 GB/sec, while Redis SET operations sustain 77.33 million operations per second. For lightweight machine learning inference, prompt processing with a small 135M model achieved 4,309.5 tokens per second. Performance drops to middle-tier levels during large-model LLM execution (14.93 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 70B model) and uncached large-block reads (151.99 GB/sec), bounded by raw RAM bandwidth rather than compute availability.

With its 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation, the D48als_v7 represents a compute-dense design tailored to scale multi-threaded execution without paying for excess memory capacity. While the absence of local disks demands remote storage overhead, the high clock speed and modern instruction set deliver efficient throughput for CPU-heavy tasks. The instance fits high-throughput web serving, CI/CD code compilation, compression pipelines, and distributed compute workloads requiring high core density.
